sections.title: Letter C
paragraphs: The letter (C) /ʃ/ makes two main sounds. Its most common sound is heard in the word (cat) /kæt/, which means a small pet that meows. The letter can also make a soft hiss or stay completely silent. It has three different sounds across English words.

sections.title: Pronouncing letter C
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to touch the soft roof. Stop the air and release it quickly. The throat does not vibrate because the voice is off. For the second sound, put the tip of your tongue near the ridge behind your upper teeth. Blow air through the tiny gap to make a continuous hiss. Place a hand on your throat to feel that it does not shake.

sections.title: Spelling rules for C
paragraphs: Before the vowels a, o, or u, this letter sounds like the plosive in (cup) /kʌp/. It also takes this sound before another consonant. Before the vowels e, i, or y, it sounds like the voiceless hiss in (city) /sɪ.ti/ or (cent) /sɛnt/. In some special words, it becomes a silent letter, as in (muscle) /mʌs.əl/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with C
paragraphs: Do not confuse the two sounds of this letter. Read the following vowel carefully before speaking. Do not add a voice when you release the stop or make the hiss. Keep your vocal cords still and let only pure air escape.
